text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1.4% today after a two-week climb, as crude oil prices pulled back on hopes for diplomatic progress in the Middle East. The company refines crude into gasoline and diesel, so when oil prices weaken—U.S. crude is down from the spike earlier this week—the margins refiners earn tend to compress. US refineries are running at 93.4% capacity, and diesel storage levels remain tight at 104.3 million barrels, which normally supports margins, but broader oil market relief outweighed that today.

The stock is caught between two conflicting pressures right now. On one hand, Ukraine's ongoing strikes on Russian diesel production and Houthi attacks on Saudi facilities have kept crude volatility high and tight. On the other hand, any sign of diplomatic calm in the Middle East—as traders are hoping for this week—pulls prices down immediately, which cuts into refinery profits. The two-week gain of 5.9% reflects that tension: the stock bounced hard on supply-side threats, but it's giving some of that back as geopolitical risk recedes momentarily.
